'''Hee Oh''' ({{langx|ko|오희}}, born 27 October 1969) is a Korean American [[mathematician]] and the Abraham Robinson Professor of Mathematics at [[Yale University]].<ref>[http://news.yale.edu/2015/04/06/hee-oh-designated-abraham-robinson-professor-mathematics Hee Oh designated the Abraham Robinson Professor of Mathematics], Yale News, April 6, 2015, retrieved 2015-04-07.</ref> She has made contributions to [[dynamical systems]], discrete subgroups of [[Lie groups]], and their connections to [[geometry]] and [[number theory]].

==Career==
She graduated with a bachelor's degree from [[Seoul National University]] in 1992 and obtained her Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1997 under the guidance of [[Gregory Margulis]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=14939 Hee Oh at Math Genealogy Project]</ref> She held several faculty positions, including ones at [[Princeton University]], [[California Institute of Technology]] and [[Brown University]], before joining the Department of Mathematics at [[Yale University]] in 2013 as the first female tenured professor in Mathematics there.<ref>[http://english.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2013/05/30/2013053001636.html "Korean becomes Yale's 1st female math professor"], ''[[The Chosun Ilbo]]'', retrieved 2013-10-30</ref> She served as Vice President of the [[American Mathematical Society]], February 1, 2021 – January 31, 2024.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=2020 Election Results|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202102/rnoti-p270.pdf?_zs=Xf5BH1&_zl=cse86|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=68|pages=270}}</ref>

==Work==
She has worked extensively on counting and [[equidistribution]] for [[Apollonian gasket|Apollonian circle packings]], [[Sierpinski carpet]]s and [[Schottky dance]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | first1=Hee | last1=Oh | first2=Nimish | last2=Shah | title=The asymptotic distribution of circles in the orbits of Kleinian groups | journal=[[Invent. Math.]] | volume=187 | year=2012 | issue=1 | pages=1–35 | mr=2874933 | doi=10.1007/s00222-011-0326-7| arxiv=1004.2130 | bibcode=2012InMat.187....1O | s2cid=115163894 }}</ref> Her recent work continues to be centered around the exploration and use of [[lie group]]s. More specifically, working with [[Representations of Lie groups|representations]] by using discrete sub groups, like [[Anosov Groups]]. Her research explores how these sub groups are useful in measuring characteristics of dynamical systems like maximal entropy.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Kim |first1=Dongryul M. |title=Relatively Anosov groups: finiteness, measure of maximal entropy, and reparameterization |date=2025-05-23 |eprint=2404.09745 |last2=Oh |first2=Hee |class=math.DS }}</ref>

==Honours==
Hee Oh was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]] in 2010, and gave a joint invited address at the 2012 AMS-MAA Joint Mathematics Meeting.<ref>[http://www.jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2012/2138_invited.html 2012 AMS-MAA Joint Mathematics Meeting]</ref> In 2012 she became an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-07.</ref>  She is the 2015 recipient of the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Browse Prizes and Awards|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/pabrowse.cgi?purl=satter-prize|access-date=2020-11-06|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref> In 2017, she was named a [[Guggenheim fellow]].
In 2018, she received the [[Ho-Am Prize]] for Science.
In 2024, she was inducted into the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>[https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2024 New Academy Members]</ref>

She served on the [[Fields Medal]] committee at the 2018 ICM in Rio. She is on the [[Abel Prize]] committee for 2024-2026.

==Selected publications==
*with [[Laurent Clozel]], Emmanuel Ullmo: Hecke operators and equidistribution of Hecke points, Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 144, 2001, pp.&nbsp;327–351
*Uniform pointwise bounds for matrix coefficients of unitary representations and applications to Kazhdan constants, Duke Mathematical Journal, vol. 113, 2002, pp.&nbsp;133–192
*with [[Alex Eskin]], [[Shahar Mozes]]: On uniform exponential growth for linear groups, Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 160, 2005, pp.&nbsp;1–30
* Proceedings of International Congress of Mathematicians (2010): ''Dynamics on geometrically finite hyperbolic manifolds with applications to Apollonian circle packings and beyond'' {{ArXiv|1006.2590}}
*with Alex Kontorovich: Apollonian circle packings and closed horospheres on hyperbolic 3-manifolds, Journal of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 24, 2011, pp.&nbsp;603–648
*with Nimish Shah: The asymptotic distribution of circles in the orbits of Kleinian groups, Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 187, 2012, pp.&nbsp;1–35
*with Nimish Shah: Equidistribution and counting for orbits of geometrically finite hyperbolic groups, Journal of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 26, 2013, pp.&nbsp;511–562
*with Amir Mohammadi: Ergodicity of unipotent flows and Kleinian groups, Journal of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 28, 2015, pp.&nbsp;531–577
*with Dale Winter: Uniform exponential mixing and resonance free regions for convex cocompact congruence subgroups of SL_2(Z), Journal of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 29, 2016, pp.&nbsp;1069–1115
*with [[Curtis McMullen]], Amir Mohammadi: Geodesic planes in hyperbolic 3-manifolds, Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 209, 2017, pp.&nbsp;425–461
*with Dale Winter: Prime number theorems and holonomies for hyperbolic rational maps, Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 208, 2017, pp.&nbsp;401–440
